data.name: Farhata
data.gender_notes: Farhata is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is given a gift or a blessing. The name Farhata carries the meaning “Gift, Grace, Blessing” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Farhata usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, grace, blessing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sign of Allah's grace and blessings
data.etymology: Farhata belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift, Grace, Blessing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farhata total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: فرحاتة
in_arabic.meaning: فرحاتة تعني الفرح والسرور في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم فرحاتة مشتق من الفعل فرح يفرح فرحا وفرحة، ويعني الفرح والسرور والابتهاج، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: 'وفرحوا بما عندهم من العلم'، ويعتبر اسم فرحاتة من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني جميلة وطيبة في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: فرحاتہ
in_urdu.meaning: فرحاتہ کا مطلب ہے خوشی اور مسرت
in_urdu.long_meaning: فرحاتہ نام عربی زبان کے الفاظ 'فرح' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے خوشی اور مسرت، یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے درمیان میں ایک مقبول نام ہے، اور اسلامی ثقافت میں اس کا بڑا احترام ہے

in_hindi.name: फ़रहाता
in_hindi.meaning: फ़रहाता का अर्थ है खुशी और आनंद
in_hindi.long_meaning: फ़रहाता नाम अरबी भाषा के शब्दों से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है खुशी और आनंद, यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में एक पारंपरिक और सम्मानित नाम है, जो इस्लामी संस्कृति में गहराई से जुड़ा हुआ है

in_pashto.name: فرحاته
in_pashto.meaning: فرحاته د خوښۍ او مسرت معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: فرحاته نوم د عربي کلمو څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې د خوښۍ او مسرت معنی لري، دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ټولنو کې یو مشهور نوم دی، او د اسلامي کلتور په چوکاټ کې یې لوی احترام دی

in_english.name: Farhata
in_english.meaning: Farhata means joy, happiness, and delight
in_english.long_meaning: The name Farhata originates from the Arabic root 'f-r-ḥ', which conveys meanings of joy, happiness, and delight, referenced in the Quran, this name holds significant spiritual and cultural value in Islamic tradition, symbolizing positive attributes and personality traits

data.cultural_impact: The name "Farhata" holds immense significance in the Islamic culture. It is a beautiful name that evokes emotions of gratitude, blessings, and prosperity. Persons bearing this name are often perceived as those who have been granted a unique prosperity, talent, or blessing. They may be viewed as being fortunate, favored, or even blessed by God. In many Islamic communities, it is common for parents to give this name to their child as a way of expressing their deepest hopes and aspirations for their offspring and their belief that they have been given a special gift or blessing.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Farhata" also carries profound spiritual significance for Muslims. It serves as a constant reminder of the belief that every good thing, including the gift of life itself, comes from Allah, the Almighty. It motivates the bearer of this name to be mindful of their blessings and to use them in the service of God and humanity. This name can also serve as an inspiration for the pursuit of knowledge, as the word "Farhana" is also used to describe a person who is seeking knowledge. By embodying this name's spiritual significance, individuals can lead fulfilling, meaningful lives that are centered on striving for personal growth and everlasting blessings from Allah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Farhata: Carrier of Joy and Delight. In the heart of every Farhata lies the ability to bring happiness and uplift those around them. Their name is a reminder to spread joy and positivity in the world.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, Chapter 2, Section 2: 'The Propagators of the Faith and the Founders of the Islamic State'. Farhata b. Al-Yamuri is mentioned as one of the military commanders who led the Muslim conquests in Iberia and North Africa.
historical_references.context: Muslim conquests and early Islamic state in Iberia and North Africa

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi, The History of the Prophets and Kings of Egypt, Volume II: 'The Ayyubids and Rulers of Egypt'. Farhata b. Salah al-Din al-Bursi is mentioned as the Ayyubid sultan of Egypt from 1229 to 1237 AD.
